items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: One of them is in the Good For Nothing by Carlisle Blackwell. He was the leading man.

ctx.x: Well you mentioned Pierron's band and what type of music they play. I forgot to mention it was in the year about 1915. I think Pierron then used mostly string instruments. And he played regular conventional ragtime like I had right on records that was of that date of error. There's some things I'd like to tell you that I may have forgotten to mention. We played for two silent movies. One of them is in the Good For Nothing by Carlisle Blackwell. He was the leading man. And her shot was Charlie Chapman. This would…

This is a letter. It says, It says, From A.J. P. Ron, 1734 Annette Street, New Orleans, Louisiana. The dateline is August 13, 1922. Mr. D. James LaRocca, original Dixon and Jazz Band. 421 Sheets Head Bay Road, Brooklyn, New York. My dear Mr. LaRocca, yours of the fifth INST comp was received and very sorry indeed for the delay and great suspense that you no doubt suffered. But only to the fact that I was out of the city, I was unable to answer at once. But I assure you that I have taken great interest in saying,…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: All the great actors come there, Carlisle Blackwell Charlie Chaplin

ctx.x: What was his name again? Carter?

Earl Carter. Yeah. A Chicago drummer. He filled in for two weeks. And Spobara comes up and takes his place. This man knew that that's all the way we used him for two weeks. And we did pretty good at the Del Abbey. Then Harry James buys an entrance in the Casino Gardens with Aikenbar and Reeves. And he approaches us and offers us $75 a week to play in the Casino Gardens. We went and played the Casino Gardens. That was Kinzen Clock. And that band was Spobara. Nunes was still with us. And Edwards, Regas, and myself.…

Over the Shilly cafe was made June. I mean March April and May And in June We work at the lab it could be in July It worked there to the last last part of December with shields This is the band that got the name original Dixieland jazz band Because prior to that we had no building We were building at this place as the original Dixieland jazz band by Harry James Cards were given out there may have been notices in the paper. I don't know now They had many musicians who went and played at this place that we left at…
